text:
sana: Quick flag - several new users reported the JS sample app crashing during onboarding. It used to work but after the exports map change their build fails at runtime.

sana: Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module when running node dist/index.js (they're on Node 16/18).

liam: Did the sample switch to referencing the package via a bare subpath? Bundlers like esbuild/vite will follow the exports map and may pick the wrong file if we don't provide both import/require.

sana: Repro steps from user: clone, npm ci, npm run start -> immediate failure. They showed package.json snippet: "exports": {"./entry": "./dist/index.mjs"}, "main": "dist/index.cjs.js" and no conditional mapping.

robin: Sounds like editor/TS resolution confusion too. Without a types entry in exports TS might resolve differently and autogenerate incorrect import paths in their starter code.

liam: Short-term fix: provide conditional exports for ./entry with both "import" and "require" targets and add a top-level "types" field. Example: { "./entry": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js" }, "types": "dist/index.d.ts" }

pat: Can we add an integration job that installs the published package into the examples folder and runs node require + dynamic import + vite build? Would catch regressions early.

ci-bot: CI: examples/integration -> exports-resolution-matrix failed 1 check.

sana: I'll open a patch with the exports change + add the CI matrix. Also draft a short onboarding note: "If you're deploying to edge or ESM-only hosts, prefer import entry; otherwise ensure conditional exports." Tagging @liam for quick review.

liam: Thanks. Also add a one-line migration note to CHANGELOG about exports map behavior and edge bundlers.

robin: and add an example in the onboarding README showing both import and require usage so users can copy-paste.
